clue.text: Required by writer — from press-cutting agency?

definitions.text: Required by writer — from press-cutting agency?

parts.words: Required by writer — from press-cutting agency?
parts.note: an office writer needs a small wire fastener for sheets, and a cuttings agency sends out cut snippets of newsprint, read as a compound

explanation.surface: Something a journalist needs, supplied perhaps by an agency that sends out press cuttings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the two halves of the hyphenated answer separately: a 'paper clip' is also a clipping from a newspaper, the stock in trade of a press-cutting agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bent wire fastener holds sheets together, standard desk kit for anyone writing.

clue.text: Aristocrat set free one caught in a trap

indicators.note: set free means the letters are released from their order and rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A nobleman released after being snared in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' is the anagram signal over I, C and IN A TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble of ancient Rome, and so anyone of high birth.

clue.text: Temporary stop some beastly supporters talking

indicators.note: talking signals the word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: an animal stands on its feet, the paws

explanation.surface: A brief halt while some animals' legs are discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief break in activity is a temporary stop.

clue.text: Adjust a rule — get cracking!

indicators.note: cracking means the preceding words are broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: An order to amend a regulation quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get cracking' reads as 'hurry up', but 'cracking' alone is the anagram signal and 'get' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate a mechanism is to adjust its setting.

clue.text: Mitigating fast, including one I have shortened

indicators.note: including signals the fast holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: shortened means I have is contracted, as in the written I've

explanation.surface: Easing a fast by cutting back on what one has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' contracts I HAVE to I'VE, dropping HA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenitive remedy soothes or eases pain, so it is softening or alleviating.

clue.text: Choose French joiner for strikers' aid

parts.note: to pick is to choose
et is French for and, a joining word

explanation.surface: Selecting a carpenter from France to help striking workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter; here it is a conjunction, the French for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickets stand outside a workplace to support a strike and dissuade workers from entering.

clue.text: Drink, said the Lord High Executioner

indicators.note: said signals that the name spoken aloud gives the answer's sound

parts.note: Ko-Ko is the Lord High Executioner in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado

explanation.surface: A drink, announced by the comic official from a Victorian operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: Ko-Ko holds the title Lord High Executioner of Titipu in The Mikado, a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; his name is pronounced like the hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from cacao powder is a common bedtime drink.

clue.text: Conrad's opportunity

explanation.definitionFit: A Joseph Conrad novel takes the title, and a favourable opportunity is a lucky break.

clue.text: Tea bar put up — can possibly provide transport

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word bar is written upwards
possibly signals the letters of can may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tea stall erected, then a coach laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns BAR to RAB; 'possibly' turns CAN to ANC. A charabanc is an old open motor coach for outings.
explanation.definitionFit: An early open motor coach used for excursions is a form of passenger transport.

clue.text: On the look-out for a drink? Right

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone watchful, hoping for a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and wary of danger is being alert.

clue.text: Grunted when making stroke

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of the preceding word are made into something new

explanation.surface: A swimmer grunted with effort while performing a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange GRUNTED. The answer is an old swimming stroke, an overarm crawl with a scissor kick named after John Trudgen.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a swimming stroke, a forerunner of the front crawl.

clue.text: Homely word-play?

parts.note: a party game played at home in which a word is acted out syllable by syllable

explanation.definitionFit: The parlour game of acting out a word's syllables is a play on words staged in the living room.

clue.text: Perfect student's afterthought

parts.note: the word is read as after plus thought, and a thought is an idea
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A model pupil's late addition to an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'afterthought' as 'after thought': the student (L, from the learner plate) comes after the thought, IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless and exactly as it should be is perfect, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Incisive war defence worker

parts.note: a trench is a dug defensive ditch in warfare
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued labourer digging fortifications in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant criticism is sharp and cutting, just as an incisive remark is.

clue.text: Sluggish in voice, perhaps

parts.note: in grammar the active is one voice of a verb, the passive being the other

explanation.surface: Someone sounding lethargic when speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice' is the grammatical term: verbs have an active and a passive voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle, not moving or doing anything, as a sluggish person is.

clue.text: Wanted by some friendly bell-ringer?

parts.note: a visitor ringing a doorbell wants to be let in, read as a church bell-ringer

explanation.definitionFit: Being let into a house is what a caller pressing the doorbell hopes for.

clue.text: House painter swindle?

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword painter
an MP is a member of the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A decorator who cheats his customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House painter' looks like a decorator, but splits into House (MP, as in the House of Commons) and painter (RA, a Royal Academician), with the painter written first.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a ramp is a racket or fraudulent scheme, especially one that overcharges.

clue.text: Fierce animals embarrassing to drapers

indicators.note: embarrassing means the letters are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: Wild beasts causing shame to cloth merchants.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that hunt and kill others for food are often fierce.

clue.text: Bearing a kind of clock

definitions.meaning: deportment, the way one holds oneself
a small portable clock in a handled case

explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is how a person holds themself, and a portable travelling timepiece takes the same name.

clue.text: Adherent is without money a punctilious person

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the adherent surrounds the money

parts.note: a sticker is something that adheres
L stands for pound, money

explanation.surface: A loyal follower without funds is fussy about detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. L is the pound sign, from Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact correctness in details, so a fussy rule-follower.

clue.text: Call for a celebrity

definitions.meaning: to call someone something is to give them a label
a famous person, a big star in a field

explanation.definitionFit: To call is to give a label, and a famous person is a big one in their field.

clue.text: A tiny bit of quiet writing

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
an article is a piece of writing in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Just a scrap of hushed prose.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute fragment or speck of matter is a tiny bit.

clue.text: What artist's model must do after this rest?

definitions.text: What artist's model must do after this rest?

parts.words: What artist's model must do after this rest?
parts.note: after a break a sitter takes the posture again, read as a re- prefix

explanation.definitionFit: Repose means rest, and split it reads as striking a posture once more.

clue.text: Concedes that a note has upset prophet

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for prophet is turned upside down

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: Someone admits a letter has troubled a soothsayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede a point is to accept it, a verbal synonym.

clue.text: Fare disliked by team?

definitions.meaning: a fare is someone who pays to travel
a member who does not pull their weight is resented by the rest of the side

explanation.definitionFit: A cab's paying traveller is a fare, and a team member who contributes nothing is carried by teammates.

clue.text: Perhaps leaves producer of machinery

definitions.meaning: a green growing thing grows foliage

explanation.definitionFit: A green growing thing puts out leaves, and industrial equipment in a factory goes by the same name.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying many a girl

indicators.note: carrying signals that the vehicle holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword many

explanation.surface: A car crammed with lots of people picking up a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a girl's first name, as girl often stands for in crosswords.

clue.text: Point of view of a pre-Norman invader

definitions.meaning: one of the Germanic tribe settling in Britain before the Normans

explanation.definitionFit: A perspective on a matter is a viewpoint, and the Germanic tribes settling England gave it its name.

clue.text: Like fat princess returning puzzle

indicators.note: returning signals that the princess's name is read backwards

parts.note: Princess Ida is the title character of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera
to pose is to puzzle or baffle

explanation.surface: An overweight princess comes back with a riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns IDA into ADI. Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan heroine, which fits this setter's Mikado clue at 6.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fatty tissue, so the word means fatty.

clue.text: Brisk as one sung by Milton

definitions.meaning: a musical tempo marking meaning lively and quick
Milton's poem L'Allegro celebrates the cheerful man

explanation.definitionFit: A lively musical tempo is brisk, and Milton's poem L'Allegro sings of the cheerful man.

clue.text: Some forgotten secret of the past, for example

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A half-remembered secret from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Past is one grammatical form of verbs marking time, alongside present and future.

clue.text: Characteristic of certain cliffs in Kent

definitions.meaning: steep cliffs have the quality of being perpendicular
a town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, south-east England

explanation.definitionFit: Steepness is the quality of a vertical cliff face, and the same word names a port town in the county of Kent.
